newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering shares boosted by buyback plans.
newsitem.headline: Schering shares boosted by buyback plans.

text.p: Shares in German pharmaceutical group Schering AG outperformed on Wednesday after the company released first quarter figures and sparked market interest by saying it would buy back its own shares.
Analysts said Schering had been generally considered a likely candidate to buy back its own shares, as its cash flow position was good and it did not seem to be seeking any major acquisitions.
"In many ways the buyback was to be expected but it seems to have triggered speculative buys," said Andreas Schmidt, chemicals analyst at BZW Deutschland, who has a buy recommendation on Schering.
"The numbers themselves were nothing special, in fact just slightly below our expectations, but the share had also underperformed in the past few days and is catching up now," Schmidt added.
Schering's shares outpaced the broader market to rise by 4.90 marks, or three percent, at 165.90 marks at 0939 GMT, having earlier hit a high of 166.50 marks.
The blue chip DAX index was up 1.6 percent.

The company said its profits had risen 10 to 15 percent in the first quarter and group sales were up 21 percent. Profit growth for the whole year would be in line with the first quarter, providing exchange rates stayed favourable.
Schering also said it planned to buy back its own shares as soon as a change in German law made this feasible.
The company also said its current market value was 11 billion marks, making it too expensive to be a lucrative takeover target.
